Title: Melaka polls: Pas, Umno must close old wounds and strengthen ties
Article:
MELAKA: Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said party members and their Umno counterparts should put aside their past political differences and focus on strengthening cooperation ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Acknowledging that the two parties had been bitter political rivals for decades, he said past disagreements should not be allowed to undermine their renewed cooperation under the Perikatan Nasional-Barisan Nasional alliance.
He also admitted to frequently criticising Umno during previous election campaigns, saying such attacks were part of the political rivalry at the time.
"If we want to preserve this political cooperation and unity, we should not keep bringing up the past.
"Close that chapter and look ahead. If we keep bringing up old issues, it will only reopen old wounds," he told reporters after attending the Ceramah Kelompok UDM Pantai Cheng last night.
Tuan Ibrahim said both parties should learn from their past disagreements and move forward to strengthen their political cooperation.
"I, too, have criticised Umno many times in my speeches in the past.
"Of course, we were political opponents then. Surely, we couldn't be praising Umno while campaigning against them.
"That was our political position at the time. For our past mistakes, we apologise, and we move forward.
"What matters now is looking ahead because the challenges before us are enormous," he said.
He said the renewed cooperation between Pas and Umno was particularly important as both parties prepared for GE16.
Tuan Ibrahim also thanked Umno and BN leaders for their willingness to work alongside PN throughout the Melaka election campaign.
He said the level of cooperation between the two coalitions had been encouraging, particularly among their respective grassroots election machinery.
"I am deeply touched by the cooperation shown by our friends in Barisan Nasional, particularly Umno leaders who have come down to work together.
"I have experienced this cooperation in Negri Sembilan, but it is even stronger here in Melaka," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Kong court sentences activist Joshua Wong to 10 years on national security charge
Article:
HONG KONG: Activist Joshua Wong, 30, who became the international face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 years in jail on a charge of collusion with foreign entities under the city's national security law.
Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and others in 2020 to request that foreign countries, institutions, organisations or individuals outside China impose sanctions or blockades, or engage in other hostile activities directed against the governments of Hong Kong and China.
He pleaded guilty to the charge in September.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Minimum wage, targeted assistance part of broader economic balancing act: Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's minimum wage policy cannot be viewed in isolation but should be seen as complementing the targeted assistance, subsidy rationalisation and affordable healthcare measures to ensure workers' income gains translate into improved household well-being, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Wage improvements are designed to move alongside initiatives such as the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), rationalisation of RON95 fuel subsidies and the upcoming MediAsas medical insurance and takaful scheme, providing a more comprehensive approach to addressing the cost of living, he posted in his LinkedIn account in relation to views he recently shared on a financial podcast.
In Budget 2027, the minimum wage will increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 monthly from June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers, while the SARA assistance has been extended to nearly 13 million Malaysians, including the M40 group.
As of Oct 22, RM3.6 billion had been disbursed to the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients through three payment phases. In total, nearly RM12 billion in STR and SARA assistance had been channelled to eligible recipients.
The allocation for STR and SARA will be increased to RM16 billion in 2027, with the monthly SARA assistance being raised to RM150, or RM1,800 annually.
The government has also scheduled the launch of MediAsas, an affordable medical insurance and takaful option, for late January 2027, as part of efforts to improve access to healthcare protection.
Besides that, RM200 million has been allocated to strengthen outsourced patient treatment programmes to reduce waiting times.
Amir Hamzah said none of these measures should be regarded as a standalone achievement, as each serves to counterbalance other economic considerations.
"None of these is a standalone win. Each one is a counterweight to something else," he said.
Amir Hamzah said the government is ultimately working towards two key objectives, namely building a sustainable economy and preserving social cohesion.
On economic sustainability, he said difficult decisions involving subsidies, fiscal discipline and revenue adequacy could not continually be deferred, as doing so would shift the burden to future generations.
"Every time we avoid a hard decision on subsidies, on fiscal discipline, on revenue adequacy, we are borrowing against our children's future. That is not something I am willing to do," he said.
On social cohesion, Amir Hamzah said that widening income inequality could eventually develop into a deeper social problem if left unaddressed.
"If the gap between the top and the bottom continues to widen, we are not just looking at an economic problem. We are manufacturing a social one," he said.
He cautioned that inequality could have far-reaching consequences that would be more difficult to address than through direct financial assistance.
"Inequality, if left unaddressed, will surface in ways that are much harder to fix than a cash handout. Just look at the devastation inequality has caused in so many other countries. We cannot let Malaysia go down that path," he said.
Amir Hamzah said this broader consideration guides the government's decisions on targeted subsidies, broadening the tax base and improving wages while ensuring households remained protected.
He said these measures should not be assessed solely based on their immediate individual impact, but on how they complement and balance one another.
"None of these can be fairly evaluated on their single, immediate impact. The real question is always: what is it offsetting? What does it balance?" he said.
Drawing a comparison with conducting an orchestra, Amir Hamzah said managing an economy requires different policies to move in tandem and at the appropriate time.
"Keeping an economy on an even keel is not like pulling a single lever. It is more like conducting an orchestra. Everything has to move together, each section coming in at the right time, to make good music," he said.

Title: Malacca Securities Sees 63.6pct upside for Impact Capital, sets 36 sen fair value
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malacca Securities has assigned a fair value of 36 sen per share to Impact Capital Holdings Bhd, representing a potential upside of 63.6 per cent from its initial public offering (IPO) price of 22 sen.
In its IPO note, the research house said the valuation was based on a target price-to-earnings (PE) multiple of 15.2 times its estimated core earnings per share (EPS) of 2.39 sen for financial year 2028 (FY28).
It said Impact Capital was well-positioned to benefit from Sarawak's ongoing digital infrastructure development, supported by its established presence in the state's information and communications technology (ICT) sector.
"With a 21-year track record in networks where reliability matters more than price, we see Impact Capital as the partner of choice for the next phase of Sarawak's digital infrastructure," it said.
The Sarawak-based ICT systems integrator provides telecommunications networks, enterprise networks, data centres and security systems, primarily for state government bodies and utility providers.
Malacca Securities said ICT integration contributed 72.7 per cent of the group's FY26 revenue, while Sarawak accounted for 75.1 per cent.
It projected the group's net profit to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 17.3 per cent, reaching RM10.7 million in FY27, RM12.3 million in FY28 and RM15.1 million in FY29.
The projected growth is expected to be driven by annual order book replenishment of RM200 million to RM250 million, higher contributions from recurring maintenance and software income, and margin expansion as the group shifts towards services and in-house delivery.
The research house noted that Impact Capital had an outstanding order book of RM169.9 million, of which RM133.7 million was scheduled for recognition by June 2027, providing earnings visibility into FY27.
It added that Sarawak's ongoing digital infrastructure development presented a multi-year growth opportunity for the group.
The state had 4,217 operational telecommunications towers as of Nov 2023, compared with an estimated 7,000 needed by 2030 to achieve full coverage of populated areas.
Meanwhile, 5G coverage stood at 63.8 per cent of populated areas in Sarawak, compared with 82.4 per cent nationally, while only 34 per cent of households had fixed broadband access, below the national average of 48 per cent.
Malacca Securities said the infrastructure gaps, coupled with continued government funding for digitalisation initiatives, would support demand for the group's services.
Impact Capital's IPO is scheduled to be listed on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 24.

Title: Negri Sembilan Education Department probes viral video of 'zombie-like' student
Article:
NILAI: The Negri Sembilan Education Department is investigating a viral video showing a student in a zombie-like state at a secondary school in the district.
Its director, Khalidah Omar, said the department was conducting further investigations before issuing a statement.
The video, which went viral on Threads, carried claims that the student, purportedly a Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate, was under the influence of a substance known as "piu piu".
The incident has also raised questions about how the substance, if drugs were indeed involved, could have been brought into the school.
The video showed the student standing near a table in a classroom, bent forward with his head lowered and seemingly motionless.
Several classmates appeared to be watching him, while a number of male students in school uniforms were seen recording the incident.
The footage drew various reactions from social media users, many of whom expressed shock over the alleged incident, particularly as it was said to have occurred within school grounds.
However, the authenticity of the claims and the location of the incident have yet to be verified.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOI Corp's solar power venture to unlock land bank potential
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd's venture into large-scale solar energy with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is expected to unlock value from its land assets while providing a new source of recurring income, says CIMB Securities.
The research house views the venture positively, saying it could enhance returns from IOI Corp's land bank and support its long-term earnings diversification strategy.
"We estimate the project could generate annual net profit of RM50 to RM60 million. This implies an RM12.5 to RM15 million contribution to IOI, based on its 25 per cent stake, excluding lease income," it said in a note.
CIMB Securities estimated that the project could generate a combined annual net profit contribution and lease rental income of RM22 million to RM24.5 million from 2029.
IOI Corp had announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd, entered into a joint venture with TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd (TRe) and a consortium of 12 small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
The partnership will develop a 500-megawatt alternating current (MWac) solar photovoltaic project integrated with a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Bahau, Negri Sembilan.
Under the arrangement, IOI Corp will hold a 25 per cent stake in the project, while TRe will own 70 per cent and the SME consortium the remaining five per cent.
CIMB Securities said the project, estimated to cost RM2 billion, would be funded through 80 per cent debt and 20 per cent equity, translating into an estimated equity investment of RM100 million by IOI Corp.
The project is backed by a 21-year renewable energy offtake agreement between TNB and DayOne Data Centres Ltd, with commercial operations targeted to begin in 2028.
In addition to its equity participation, IOI Corp will lease 526.09 hectares of oil palm land to the joint venture, providing an additional recurring income stream while retaining ownership of the land.
CIMB Securities maintained its earnings forecasts and sum-of-parts-based target price of RM5.03 for IOI Corp, with its 'Buy' recommendation unchanged.
The research firm estimated annual rental income of RM9.5 million, based on an assumed rental rate of RM18,000 per hectare for the 526-hectare site.
It said the rental income would exceed the RM8,000 to RM9,000 per hectare currently generated from plantation operations, although the actual rental rate was not disclosed.
CIMB Securities also said the venture offered a scalable model for unlocking value from IOI Corp's land bank, although it was unlikely to materially change the group's near-term earnings profile.
The project was expected to deliver an equity internal rate of return of between nine and 10 per cent, it added.

Title: Anwar: Differences of opinion between ministries do not mean government is divided
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Differences in views or approaches between ministries do not reflect divisions within the government, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said such differences were part of the policy discussion and deliberation process, taking into account each ministry's responsibilities, jurisdiction and priorities to ensure the effective implementation of the government's agenda.
Anwar said the government ensured proper coordination between ministries to maintain policy consistency, avoid overlapping functions and ensure decisions were guided by public interest, national development priorities and the government's financial capacity.
"At the same time, the country's economic performance is continuously monitored based on current data and economic indicators.
"This is to assess the effectiveness of policies implemented and ensure the resilience of the national economy is strengthened in facing global economic uncertainties," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on the parliament website today.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin (PN-Larut), who asked whether open disagreements between the Finance Ministry and the Rural and Regional Development Ministry indicated divisions within the government, and who had the final say on the government's official position.
Anwar said that, to ensure effective governance, all government policies and decisions must undergo the necessary deliberation and coordination.
"Matters requiring collective decisions will be brought before the Cabinet for consideration and approval, in line with the principle of collective Cabinet responsibility.
"Accordingly, the government will continue to strengthen cooperation between ministries, improve policy implementation and monitor the progress of each initiative.
"This is to ensure decisions translate into tangible, sustainable outcomes that benefit the people," he said.
Previously, Lim Guan Eng questioned the Rural and Regional Development Ministry's spending on rural road projects, which he claimed had exceeded the original allocation by RM2.1 billion between 2023 and 2025.
However, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi clarified that the original allocation for the period was RM3.982 billion before being revised to RM6.143 billion, while actual expenditure stood at RM6.108 billion.
On Oct 29, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the Finance Ministry had approved an additional RM500 million for the ministry through an Expenditure Approval Letter (SKB) to help settle outstanding payments to contractors.
He said a Variation Notice (NOC) amounting to RM491 million had also been approved earlier.

Title: Tun Faisal: Bersatu stayed away from PN seat talks over legal implications
Article:
MELAKA: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) did not attend Perikatan Nasional's (PN) seat talks because participating would carry severe legal implications and validate constitutional violations committed by Pas, the party said.
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said the party's absence from the meeting, which Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man raised, was an intentional, principled decision officially communicated by Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali.
He was responding to Tuan Ibrahim, who claimed Bersatu skipped PN's seat negotiations before fielding candidates against the coalition while still claiming to be an ally.
When contacted, Tun Faisal said attending would create a misleading impression that Pas had committed no wrongdoing, effectively endorsing decisions made in breach of the coalition's constitution.
"If we attended, it would carry the legal implication that we endorse Pas's past actions as not being wrong. We lodged a complaint, and the Registrar of Societies (RoS) already meted out a punishment.
"The court did not declare that they were innocent; the court merely stayed the punishment pending a review. Attending would make it seem as though nothing happened and as if we are endorsing it," he said.
Tun Faisal also accused Pas of showing no remorse or willingness to rectify its actions, and of running PN arbitrarily since it took control of the coalition's administration from Bersatu.
"From day one, Pas has administered Perikatan Nasional in a manner that is unfair, defies procedure, breaches the constitution, and sidelines the Supreme Council.
"Decisions made during the Supreme Council meetings were unilaterally breached by the Pas president. In Negri Sembilan, it reached a level of oppression by denying Bersatu its legitimate rights as a component member of PN.
"We took this to the RoS because we demand justice. Those who committed violations must face consequences, and the situation inside PN must be set right," Tun Faisal added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian shoppers turn selective as Asean growth fails to lift FMCG spending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cautious household spending and increasingly selective shoppers are making it harder for fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in Malaysia and other Asean countries to capture growth.
This challenge arises despite resilient economic expansion across Southeast Asia, according to a new Bain & Company and NielsenIQ report.
More than 50 million people are expected to enter the consuming class by 2030, the report noted.
Covering Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, the report said FMCG companies can no longer rely on broad-based consumption growth as consumers become more deliberate about where they spend their money.
Across the six markets, FMCG value growth remained largely flat between 2023 and the first half of 2026, with weak sales volumes offsetting continued price increases.
While Southeast Asia's economy is projected to grow by 5.1 per cent in 2026, household spending faces pressure from slower real wage growth and high household debt.
The result is a more selective consumer, with shoppers increasingly willing to spend more on products they see as delivering genuine benefits while seeking savings in other categories.
"Growth in Southeast Asia is not disappearing - it is becoming harder to capture," said Praneeth Yendamuri, partner and head of Asia Pacific Consumer Products practice at Bain.
"Consumer products companies can no longer rely on broad-based consumption growth or traditional definitions of premium and value."
For Malaysian FMCG brands and retailers, the findings point to a consumer market where simply offering either the cheapest or most premium product may no longer be enough.
The report found that seven in 10 consumers who traded up in one category also traded down in another.
Beauty and baby care products are among categories seeing greater premiumisation, particularly where consumers associate products with better health, safety, performance or benefits for their families.
Household products, however, remain more value-oriented.
Overall, 58 per cent of consumers said they were willing to pay a premium for compelling reasons such as trusted quality, proven effectiveness or meaningfully better performance.
At the same time, brand loyalty is becoming increasingly conditional.
Half of Southeast Asian shoppers said they would switch brands immediately if their usual choice was unavailable.
Yendamuri said businesses would need to make sharper choices about where to compete and build products around genuine consumer willingness to pay.

Title: Motorists to enjoy 50pct toll discount for two days in conjunction with Deepavali
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount for two days in conjunction with Deepavali, with the government allocating RM20.11 million in compensation to participating highway concessionaires.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the discount would take effect from midnight this Friday until 11.59pm on Saturday.
The initiative covers Class 1 private vehicles at all toll plazas, as well as Class 2 vehicles at the Penang Bridge.
However, the discount will not apply at border toll plazas, namely the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) toll plaza on the North-South Expressway and Tanjung Kupang toll plaza on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link.
In a statement today, Nanta said the initiative reflected the government's continued commitment to safeguarding the people's welfare and well-being.
He said the discount was expected to ease travel costs, particularly for Hindus returning to their hometowns or visiting family members to celebrate Deepavali.
Motorists are advised to plan their journeys early to avoid traffic congestion.
They should also ensure their Touch 'n Go cards or eWallets have sufficient balance, observe speed limits, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles and take adequate rest to avoid driver fatigue.
Motorists are also encouraged to check the latest traffic updates and highway incidents through the Malaysian Highway Authority's official channels to better plan their journeys.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AirAsia, Capital A shares surge as oil prices plunge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aviation-related stocks surged in early trade on Thursday as a sharp decline in crude oil prices raised hopes of lower fuel costs for airlines.
AirAsia Group Bhd and Capital A Bhd emerged as Bursa Malaysia's two most actively traded counters, with both recording double-digit gains.
As at 9.30am, AirAsia Group's shares had climbed as much as 20.88 per cent, or 9.5 sen, to 55 sen from Wednesday's close of 45.5 sen.
The stock subsequently eased to 52 sen, still up 14.29 per cent, or 6.5 sen, with more than 26 million shares changing hands.
At that price, the airline's market capitalisation stood at RM1.74 billion.
Meanwhile, its associate Capital A rose as much as 15.22 per cent, or 3.5 sen, to 26.5 sen from Wednesday's close of 23 sen.
At the time of writing, Capital A was trading at 25.5 sen, up 10.87 per cent, or 2.5 sen, with more than 21 million shares traded.
The counter's market capitalisation stood at RM1.14 billion.
The gains came as global oil prices plunged on Wednesday amid growing expectations of a possible end to the US-Israeli war with Iran following the US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures for January delivery fell US$8.98, or 8.7 per cent, to settle at US$94.62 a barrel on the ICE Futures Europe exchange.
Lower oil prices could ease fuel costs for airlines, potentially improving their operating margins.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore shoppers make a beeline for Johor's Little India bazaar
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The annual Deepavali bazaar in Johor Baru's Little India has drawn local shoppers and visitors from Singapore seeking traditional snacks, clothing and other festive goods.
Its strategic location in the city centre, close to the Johor Causeway, makes it a popular destination for Singaporeans seeking a variety of items ahead of the festival.
The annual bazaar offers a wide selection of goods, including traditional snacks, clothing, home decorations and women's accessories.
Singaporean visitor T. Murthy, 78, said he and his family travelled to the city every year to buy traditional snacks sold at the bazaar.
"There is a wide variety of snacks here, including muruku, which taste very good because they are traditionally homemade.
"They are also much cheaper and more affordable than those sold in Singapore. That is why I enjoy shopping here for Deepavali," he said when met yesterday.
The bazaar also reflects the spirit of unity, with visitors from different communities taking the opportunity to shop and experience the festive preparations.
Clothing trader S. Candrika, 39, said her stall selling Punjabi attire attracted not only members of the local Indian community but also shoppers from other ethnic groups.
"We have regular customers who return to shop here every year. We also receive visits from Malay and Chinese customers who buy traditional Punjabi clothes.
"Some buy them to wear when visiting their Indian friends, while others purchase them for events with an Indian traditional theme," she said.
Another trader, J. Sathis, 31, said unpredictable weather and occasional rain in recent weeks had affected businesses to some extent.
"This area is well known and is one of the attractions for visitors during the Deepavali festive season.
"I expect the number of visitors to continue increasing as the festival approaches on Sunday," he said.S

Title: Citi employee killed in shooting at Florida office, suspect dead
Article:
NEW YORK: A Citigroup employee was killed in a shooting at the bank's office in Tampa, Florida on Wednesday, Chief Executive Jane Fraser said, while authorities said the suspect involved was also dead.
In a memo to staff, Fraser said the bank was still learning the details of what happened and was working closely with local law enforcement.
"The Tampa campus is secure, and we are adding additional security to all of our other sites as necessary," Fraser said.
Hilsboro County Sheriff Chad Chronister said in a statement earlier on Wednesday that "the suspect involved in the Citibank Active Threat scene is deceased."
The sheriff also said 365 deputies had responded and that he believed it was a targeted incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Monsoon aid brings relief to 3,000 residents in Tumpat
Article:
TUMPAT: Food and essential supplies distributed ahead of the northeast monsoon have brought relief to more than 3,000 residents in 12 villages.
Some villagers, meanwhile, have begun buying and stockpiling dry food to prepare for the monsoon season rather than relying solely on aid.
Teluk Renjuna villager Mohd Faiza Ibrahim, 46, said most residents tended to stay home during the monsoon as persistent rain and rising river levels made it difficult to travel.
"Conditions become more difficult when strong winds raise fears of falling trees, as our village is along the Kelantan River delta, which is lined with coconut trees.
"Boats are the main mode of transport for residents. If the roads remain safe, we can still travel by motorcycle. However, when floodwaters reach the village, residents have to stay at home.
"We are grateful that assistance is provided every year," he said.
Faiza was speaking during a distribution of supplies by the Social Welfare Department at the forward base in Kampung Teluk Renjuna yesterday.
The aid, comprising rice, cooking oil, sardines, sugar and tea, was transported in six boats along a 10km stretch of the Kelantan River, from the Padang Kemahkotaan jetty to the Kampung Teluk Renjuna jetty.
Grocery shop owner Mohd Husin Mohammad, 54, said he had also increased stocks at his premises ahead of the monsoon.
He said petrol was among the essential supplies needed by residents, as boats were their main mode of transport, and he had to ensure his shop maintained an adequate fuel supply.
"Even during the monsoon season and rainy weather, I have to ensure my shop has sufficient supplies. If I need to replenish stocks, I have no problem navigating my boat to the mainland to make purchases, as I am used to it.
"My other preparation is to move goods in the shop to higher ground, as floodwaters overflow onto the land and enter the premises whenever flooding occurs," he said.
Tumpat, in northern Kelantan, is home to numerous small river islands along the Kelantan River delta, where communities are vulnerable to flooding during the annual northeast monsoon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens firmer on improved global sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Thursday, tracking Wall Street's positive overnight performance as improving global sentiment and easing geopolitical concerns lifted investor confidence.
At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 11.16 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 1,627.72 from Wednesday's close of 1,616.56.
The benchmark index opened 6.72 points higher at 1,623.28.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 241 to 232, while 268 counters were unchanged, 2,020 untraded and 10 suspended.
Turnover stood at 263.87 million units worth RM148.93 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the local bourse could see renewed buying interest following the previous session's profit-taking activities, supported by lower crude oil prices and improving external sentiment.
He said Wall Street had closed sharply higher following the Democrats' significant gains in the US midterm elections, which helped ease some of the economic and geopolitical uncertainties weighing on markets.
"Back home, we believe the index may see strong buying support today, particularly as crude oil prices have retreated," he told Bernama.
Thong noted that Brent crude had weakened to below US$95 per barrel amid hopes of easing tensions in West Asia, providing support to market sentiment, with the FBM KLCI expected to trend within the 1,615 to 1,630 range today.
Among the 30 FBM KLCI constituents, 24 counters were trading higher, one lower and five unchanged.
Banking heavyweight stocks were all firmer ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia's Overnight Policy Rate decision, due later in the afternoon, with expectations of an interest rate hike lending support to the local currency.
Of the heavyweight stocks, Maybank and IHH Healthcare were 10 sen firmer at RM10.00 and RM7.88, respectively, while Public Bank rose four sen to RM4.81, CIMB gained 11 sen to RM7.02, and Tenaga Nasional was flat at RM13.14.
In active trade, AirAsia rose eight sen to 53.5 sen, Capital A gained three sen to 26 sen, while Dagang Nexchange, VS Industry and MMAG were half a sen lower at 41.5 sen, 33 sen and two sen, respectively.
Nestle led the top gainers, rising RM1.00 to RM94.50, while Hong Leong Bank gained 26 sen to RM21.50, Allianz rose 20 sen to RM19.72, Hong Leong Financial gained 18 sen to RM17.64, and PPB advanced 14 sen to RM9.00.
Among the top losers, MPI fell RM1.20 to RM39.42, Vitrox lost 36 sen to RM10.54, Hengyuan Refining dropped 32 sen to RM3.30, UWC slipped 19 sen to RM7.01, and Petronas Chemicals fell 18 sen to RM4.52.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index surged 52.26 points to 12,130.24, while the FBM Top 100 Index gained 57.67 points to 11,942.75.
The FBM Mid 70 Index fell 17.14 points to 17,494.11, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 13.78 points to 12,118.21, and the FBM ACE Index declined 15.85 points to 5,404.93.
Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.60 of a point to 177.61, while the Energy Index fell 13.91 points to 814.01. The Financial Services Index gained 200.40 points to 18,786.71, while the Plantation Index rose 45.79 points to 8,807.67.

Title: Explainer: Will Bank Negara raise OPR to 3pct? What it means for your loans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Will Bank Negara Malaysia raise interest rates today? And if it does, how much more could you end up paying on your housing loan?
The central bank will announce its final interest rate decision of the year at 3pm, with most economists expecting it to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent.
However, some believe stronger economic growth has strengthened the case for raising the OPR to three per cent, effectively reversing the pre-emptive cut made in July 2025.
Bank Negara lowered the OPR by 25 basis points last year to cushion the economy against global uncertainties, particularly US trade tariffs.
But Malaysia's economy has since performed better than expected, expanding 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, according to advance estimates.
Some economists believe this gives Bank Negara room to "normalise" interest rates by returning the OPR to its previous level.
What would a rate hike mean for your loans?
For homeowners with floating-rate mortgages, a 25-basis-point increase would generally mean higher monthly repayments.
For example, a RM300,000 outstanding housing loan with 25 years remaining and an effective interest rate of four per cent would carry monthly repayments of about RM1,584.
If the rate increases to 4.25 per cent, repayments could rise to approximately RM1,625, or RM41 more a month.
For a RM500,000 loan under the same conditions, the increase would be around RM68 a month.
These are illustrative calculations. Actual repayments depend on individual loan terms and banks' adjustments.
What about car loans and savings?
Existing fixed-rate car loans generally would not be affected, although variable-rate financing could become more expensive.
Credit card interest rates also do not automatically increase when the OPR rises.
Savers, meanwhile, could benefit from better fixed deposit returns if banks adjust their deposit rates upwards.
Will Bank Negara actually raise rates?
The majority of economists expect the central bank to hold off for now, particularly with inflation remaining manageable at 1.8 per cent in September.
Others argue that stronger growth warrants a return to three per cent to prevent borrowing costs from remaining unnecessarily low.
The debate comes as several central banks, including those in the UK and Japan, have raised interest rates this year amid renewed inflation pressures.
For Malaysia, however, the question is whether stronger growth alone is sufficient reason to reverse last year's precautionary cut.
Bank Negara's decision at 3pm could provide an important indication of where borrowing costs are headed in 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two women detained after RM3.47mil agarwood seizure in Kelantan
Article:
PASIR MAS: Two women were detained after police seized agarwood worth RM3.47 million in a raid on a house in Kampung Baharu Cherang Hangus, Chicha Tinggi.
The raid was conducted at 5pm yesterday under Op Taring Wawasan by personnel from the General Operations Force (GOF) 7th Battalion's Intelligence Branch, assisted by the Kelantan Forestry Department.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid followed surveillance and information from the public.
He said inspections of the house, a storeroom and an old factory next to the residence uncovered 197 agarwood logs and 310.8kg of agarwood pieces, as well as seven plastic drums and 11 documents.
"The two women, aged 19 and 54, were detained after producing suspicious documents relating to ownership of the items.
"The arrests and seized items were subsequently handed over to the Kelantan Forestry Department," he said.
He said initial investigations found that the premises were believed to have been operating since 2000 and had previously held a licence to collect agarwood.
"However, the licence and permit to transport the wood were found to have been terminated by the Forestry Department in 2016.
"The factory's original owner died in September, and all the agarwood was managed and kept by the family.
"The agarwood is believed to have been obtained from forests and privately owned land across Kelantan since 2016," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 84 of the National Forestry Act 1984 (Act 313) for storing agarwood without a valid licence or permit.
Agarwood, often known as 'black gold', is a highly prized fragrant wood used in luxury perfumes and incense because of its distinctive aroma and high market value.

Title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's stunning midterm defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028.
The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice-President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss.
But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars such as Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful appeal has already drawn comparisons with former president Barack Obama.
Republicans in turmoil
The MAGA coalition that propelled Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday's midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.
Long seen as the odds-on favourite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterm campaign, attending rallies in swing states.
The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump's unpopular war on Iran in a lengthy post on X on Wednesday.
But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump.
It is a familiar problem for US vice-presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice-president Kamala Harris faced a similar problem in 2024 when she said that "there's not a thing that comes to mind" when asked how she would differentiate herself from Joe Biden.
"The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice-presidents seldom win the presidency," James Lindsay of the Council on Foreign Relations said.
Trump's Secretary of State Marco Rubio's name has also been bandied about.
Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms, but any top official in Trump's administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war.
The Republicans' midterm disaster could, however, boost other possible candidates.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal.
He described the Democratic sweep as "the political equivalent of a meteor strike" and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off.
Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats' stunning Senate and gubernatorial victories in his state in the midterms.
[[nid:1571179]]
Democrats on a high
The Democratic field is crowded, but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost.
Ossoff's re-election as a Georgia senator has fuelled speculation about a 2028 run by the telegenic politician, who has already gained attention for mocking Trump's relationship with a young staffer.
The 39-year-old has said that he has "zero interest in running for president", but his swiftly declared victory in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his standing in the party.
Before the midterms, Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favourite for the nomination, but many in the party would prefer someone without a losing track record.
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed to re-election in the key battleground state.
Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. In an interview with AFP in September, he predicted that Trump's presidency "as we know it would be over after the midterms".
But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old-guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars.
A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.
Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona Senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat to discuss RON95 quality, landfill woes, foreign drivers today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The quality of RON95 petrol samples, solid waste landfill mitigation, and enforcement against foreigners driving without valid licences will take centre stage in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) will ask the domestic trade and cost of living minister to state the analysis outcome of RON95 samples across five states and depots during the Minister's Question Time.
He is also seeking details on immediate measures to restore consumer confidence and compensation for affected vehicle owners.
In the same session, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the housing and local government minister about long-term strategies for critical open dumpsites under rural local authorities, as well as mitigation plans for districts without Waste-to-Energy plants.
During the oral question-and-answer session, Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) will ask the transport minister to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms against foreigners, including United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees cardholders and undocumented immigrants, driving motor vehicles without a valid licence.
Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) will ask the home minister to outline the progress of the early detection radar system, unmanned aerial vehicles, and satellite systems, the percentage of 24-hour surveillance coverage, and critical asset capability gaps in the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency.
Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong) will query the government on its preparedness to prevent and address haze episodes, given expectations that the El Nino phenomenon will persist until mid-2027.
Following the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will proceed with the committee stage debate and ministerial replies on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 and the Motion on the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates.
The committee stage debate and winding-up session for the 2027 Budget will run until Nov 26, according to the parliamentary calendar.
The Dewan Rakyat will sit for 37 days until Dec 8.

Title: Police dismiss viral claim of teen electrocuted to death on mall massage chair
Article:
KAJANG: A viral post claiming that a teenage girl died after being electrocuted while using a massage chair at a shopping mall is false.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said investigations found no such incident had occurred.
He said police received a report at 7.50pm yesterday concerning a Facebook post carrying the claim.
"The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both upon conviction," he said in a statement.
He said the case was also being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code for statements conducing to public mischief.
Those with information or inquiries should refer to official police channels or contact the Kajang district police headquarters at 03-89114222.
The viral post featured an image, believed to be AI-generated, showing a woman purportedly dead while using a massage chair.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: French blood bank hit in latest cyberattack on fridges
Article:
PARIS: The cooling system of France's blood bank has been hit by a cyberattack similar to the hacker attack targeting refrigeration systems across Europe earlier this week, the EFS bank said on Wednesday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
Cooling rooms at three of the bank's locations have been affected, EFS said.
The refrigeration systems, supplied by an external provider, were manipulated remotely, causing operating temperatures to rise to very high levels, it said.
Temperatures rose from -30°C to 11°C, according to investigative newspaper Le Canard Enchaîné.
Thanks to monitoring and alarm systems, the rise in temperature was detected quickly and action was taken swiftly. No samples or blood products were compromised, according to EFS.
The affected systems have since been brought under control, and blood products have been transferred to other facilities as a precautionary measure, it said.
EFS stores blood products and biological samples in cooling units before they are delivered to healthcare facilities.
The incident comes after cybercriminals targeted fridges and freezers in European supermarkets, causing temperatures to rise, including in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, Luxembourg, Estonia, Finland, Germany and the Netherlands.
A similar large-scale attack in mid-October caused fridges to warm up in major French supermarket chains.
It remains unclear who was behind the attacks.

Title: Texas data centres face uncertain future after Hinojosa wins governor's race
Article:
HOUSTON/NEW YORK: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has rattled the state's data centre industry with a campaign pledge to halt new projects, injecting new uncertainty into one of the country's fastest-growing markets for server warehouses worth billions of dollars.
With plentiful energy supplies, relatively cheap land and a pro-business policy, Texas has become one of the leading regions in the world for data center developments. Big Tech companies including Meta, Google and Microsoft have announced major data center projects in the state over the past two years.
The data center industry there had already come under pressure before the midterms. On August 3, Greg Abbott became one of the first Republican governors in the US to halt the connection of new data centers to the state's electric grid amid growing opposition from rural communities and a surge in requests to connect to the state's power grid.
Abbott, who had supported data centers a month earlier, also ordered a comprehensive audit of the projects, with a focus on power demand, environmental impacts and tax breaks given to developers.
Even before Hinojosa's dramatic upset of Abbott on Tuesday, she had vowed to take the crackdown on data centers a step further by banning all data center approvals until the state legislature passes laws "to protect Texans, so that Texans have a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into our community."
By the time Texas halted data centers connecting to its grid, state grid operator ERCOT said it was tracking more than 400 gigawatts of data center projects – roughly equivalent to what it would take to power the entire US South – seeking to connect to the grid.
Abbott's about-face also threw tens of billions of dollars of data center projects planned in Texas into jeopardy and raised doubts over whether hundreds of millions in grid deposits paid by data centers seeking to connect to the grid would be returned. Since ordering the audit, Abbott has also taken actions to penalize data center water violations retroactively and temporarily banned the state from issuing air permits for the projects.
Abbott, however, did not issue a formal moratorium on data centers, which Hinojosa has vowed to do. Certain measures by Abbott also had a near-term expiration date, like the air permit ban and the audit, which was expected to conclude at the end of 2026.
The new governor's administration and the Texas legislature will now need to get up to speed on the state's patchwork of recent actions and regulations on data centers before solidifying a new set of laws and rules around the industry, said Austin McCarty, a Texas data center attorney with K&L Gates.
"It's a brand-new day in Texas for a ton of what was probably considered settled policy – not just for data centers, but energy as a whole," McCarty said.
Some Texas data center projects are likely to get delayed or to see developers exit the state entirely, while others are expected to speed up the process of completing and powering up the centers before new restrictions take hold, he added.
The Data Center Coalition, which represents Big Tech and other data center developers, said its members would continue to pursue their infrastructure build-out in the state while working with state and local governments.
"Enhancing affordability, creating jobs, and keeping the state's economy strong are top priorities for Texans. Data centers can continue to play a crucial role in advancing those priorities by bringing investment to local communities," said Jess Heck, Texas director of government affairs at the Data Center Coalition.
SWEEPING OPPOSITION
Some 42 per cent of registered voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll published this week said limiting the construction of data centers used to power AI was very important or the most important issue for them.
"The data centers connect economic development to everyday concerns," University of Houston political scientist Brandon Rottinghaus said a day before the vote, citing electricity bills, water supplies and property rights.
Polling showed rural voters, who are "at the epicenter of so many of these fights," were unhappy with the spread of data centers heading into the election, he said.
Brittany Kaiser, CEO of data center developer Alpha Compute, said the results in Texas and Ohio, where winning candidates made opposition to data centers a big part of their platforms, will make some companies question whether to invest in those states. Developers that don't already have signed contracts and financing are more likely to look elsewhere, including abroad in Canada, Mexico and Europe, she said.
"What I really think is that a lot of companies are going to be investing in very red states and purple states," Kaiser said in an interview on Wednesday. "Definitely over the past six months, that's been most of the pipeline that I've created for my own business, because it looks like less of a political risk."
Kaiser said the skepticism comes from voters' fears about AI and what data centers mean for their electricity bills, the environment and jobs, and that many AI CEOs have "not made it easy to be excited about the future of AI."
Industry efforts to keep data center costs from being passed on to ratepayers never reached voters, she said, and developers now need to engage directly with legislators, regulators and communities and go beyond regulatory compliance to be good neighbors.
"I definitely never thought data centers would be in a position where people would rather live near a nuclear facility or a prison," Kaiser said.
Some 76 per cent of voters nationwide said they opposed the construction of a new data center in their community, according to an NBC and SSRS exit poll. Ahead of the vote, a University of Houston poll in October found that 79 per cent of likely Texas voters supported limits on the number of data centers that can be built in the state.
Texas accounts for 25 per cent of planned data center capacity in the US, according to a note by Goldman Sachs. New Democratic governors in the Lone Star State and other burgeoning data center hubs, including Georgia and Michigan, could result in state legislation that would end tax breaks for the industry, tighten environmental and electricity rules and pave the way for towns and cities to pass their own moratoria, the note said.
"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Elon Musk, who supported Abbott in the election and had spent US$158 million to promote Texas Republican US Senate candidate Ken Paxton alone, wrote early Wednesday on X.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy, 6, drowned while fishing alone in Kulai pond, police rule out foul play
Article:
KULAI: Police have ruled out foul play in the
drowning of a 6-year-old boy
found in a retention pond near Taman Sungai Mas yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said initial investigations revealed the boy's parents left for work at 6.30am, leaving him asleep with his 17-year-old sister.
However, at 10am, an acquaintance contacted the mother to inform her that the child had been found unconscious in the pond, located about 50m from their home.
Firefighters retrieved the boy from the water.
Tan said investigations showed the victim was believed to have gone to the pond alone to fish, following the discovery of a fishing rod near the scene.
A medical officer pronounced the child dead at 11.15am. A post-mortem examination confirmed the cause of death as drowning.
Tan said the case has been classified as a sudden death report, with further investigations ongoing.
He advised parents and guardians to closely monitor their children and not allow them to engage in activities near high-risk areas such as ponds, rivers, and open waters without adult supervision.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dodol sales double amid Melaka election campaign
Article:
MELAKA: Sales of traditional Melaka dodol have doubled for a local producer, driven by an influx of political party campaign teams and visitors from outside the state during the 16th Melaka election campaign.
Nur Aliyah Zaidi, 28, whose family has been making dodol for four generations, said the presence of campaign teams and visitors from outside the state had contributed to an increase in customers visiting their premises.
She said many visitors from outside Melaka took the opportunity to buy dodol as souvenirs for their families, while others purchased the traditional delicacy for their own consumption.
"Most people who come to Melaka to campaign, whether from within or outside the state, will look for local favourites such as asam pedas and dodol.
"Dodol is among the traditional delicacies they seek out and buy to take home or give to their families," she said when met here today.
Nur Aliyah said visits by political party campaign teams usually increased towards the end of the campaign period, based on her family's experience in previous elections.
Some campaign teams also placed bulk orders to distribute dodol to villagers or serve it during community programmes, she added.
She said the family business was established in 1960 by her great-grandmother, the late Tijah Maakti, and had been passed down through four generations.
After Tijah's death, the business was continued by Nur Aliyah's grandmother, the late Echa Ngah, for about 15 years before her father took over when her grandmother became unwell.
Nur Aliyah said the family continued to use traditional wood-fired cooking methods, which gave the dodol its distinctive aroma and texture compared with machine-made products.
"We sell dodol in several packaging options, including jars containing 36 pieces for RM40, 500g packs for RM13 and smaller packs containing 12 pieces for RM13.
"We operate daily from 9am to 9pm and also receive visits from school students who want to see how this traditional delicacy is made," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dr Solehin says brother Dr Akmal opens doors on Bemban campaign trail
Article:
JASIN: Bersama's Bemban candidate Dr Solehin Saleh said his younger brother, Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, had helped him engage rural Malay voters.
Dr Solehin said being Dr Akmal's elder brother had opened doors during the campaign, particularly when meeting rural and elderly Malay voters.
He said he did not actively use his brother's popularity, but their family connection served as an icebreaker.
"There is no denying that Dr Akmal has huge influence, especially among the Malays," he said.
"People naturally recognise the family connection and say, 'Oh, you are Dr Akmal's brother'.
"You cannot deny blood ties, but it isn't a calculated move," he said.
Asked how his political identity differed from his outspoken brother's, Dr Solehin said their ideological approaches were "night and day". However, he said there was "zero animosity" between them despite their opposing political affiliations.
"We grew up in an Umno family, but in our house, there is a strict golden rule left behind by my late father — leave politics outside the front door.
"I have breakfast with Dr Akmal every single morning. We live together as a family to take care of our mother since my father passed away.
"We talk about his fish pond, my pygmy goats, and family matters. Never politics.
"Dr Akmal is seen as fierce and firm. I am more relaxed and moderate. He plays to his political base, but I am in the centre," he said.
"As a doctor, when patients come to see me, I don't see them as Malay, Chinese, or Indian. They share the same health and financial struggles.
"That moderate, colour-blind perspective is what I bring into politics," he said.
Dr Solehin had also made healthcare and eldercare central to his campaign, pledging to replicate his low-cost 'Ambulans Marhaen' grassroots initiative and provide home medical visits without consultation fees in Bemban.
He said an estimated 25 per cent of the constituency's population comprised senior citizens or people approaching old age, many living alone while their adult children worked elsewhere.
He said operational constraints remained a challenge, but maintained that affordable primary care was a public necessity.
"When we go to the ground and visit the villages, we encounter bedridden and elderly patients who urgently need follow-up hospital visits or house-call treatments, but their families simply cannot afford private transport," he said.
"Whether as an assemblyman or through our existing healthcare teams, this is a welfare commitment we are already doing and will continue to bring to the people of Bemban," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold rises after biggest daily gain since August, with US payrolls in focus
Article:
LONDON: Gold prices rose in early Asian trade on Thursday after posting their biggest daily gain since mid-August in the previous session, buoyed by a weaker US dollar, while investors awaited this week's non-farm payrolls report for clues on the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.
FUNDAMENTALS
Spot gold was up 0.6 per cent at US$4,082.76 per ounce by 0036 GMT, after climbing about 3.4 per cent on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.5 per cent to US$4,092.90.
The dollar retreated on Wednesday but was off its earlier lows after a sweeping victory by Democrats in the US midterm elections removed a source of uncertainty for the market while investors gauged the potential for regulatory changes.
A weaker dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies.
US private payrolls growth increased further in October, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday.
Market participants now await the US nonfarm payrolls report on Friday to further gauge the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.
On the geopolitical front, Washington's hostility towards Tehran will not change through partisan shifts or any concessions to the US, and those who believe otherwise are "greatly mistaken", Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday.
Traders currently see an 83 per cent chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
Meanwhile, Citi has a 0-3 month price target of US$4,500 per ounce for gold, it said on Wednesday, as it sees substantial upside potential if the Strait of Hormuz reopens and the Yemen/Saudi conflict de-escalates by the year-end, as it expects.
Euro zone inflation rose to a three-year high last month on surging food and energy costs and was set to rise further in the coming months, firming up the case for another European Central Bank rate hike in December.
The Bank of England is widely expected to raise interest rates for the first time in three years on Thursday due to mounting inflation pressures from the US-Iran war.
Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.3 per cent to US$52.37 per ounce, platinum gained 0.6 per cent to US$1,505.85 and palladium dropped 0.1 per cent to US$1,003.83.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Evaluate Ab Rauf's leadership based on facts, not baseless claims
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Melaka voters should focus on the state government's achievements rather than be influenced by baseless claims when deciding whom to support in the Nov 14 state election.
Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Johan Abd Aziz said caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh's administrative track record spoke for itself and should be the basis for voters to evaluate the state government.
"From the very beginning, I have told all Melaka residents not to listen to all the nonsense, but to focus on the facts.
"The facts about Rauf's achievements since becoming Chief Minister are already out there. Those are the real facts," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after delivering a campaign speech in Kampung Lubok Redan, in the Tanjung Bidara state constituency. Also present was Ab Rauf, who is Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman.
Johan, who is also Dusun Tua assemblyman, said cooperation between BN and Perikatan Nasional in Melaka was another important step towards demonstrating unity and forming a stronger government.
He said election machinery coordination across all 28 state constituencies had begun before nomination day through meetings with local leaders.
The effort would continue throughout the campaign, with the aim of strengthening ties between the two coalitions and potentially paving the way for broader cooperation at federal level.
"Melaka is very important. We are proving our unity here. If we succeed in all 28 (constituencies), this will be proof that the people of Malaysia are rising and want to see a more united government," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI push to transform government, unlock growth for Malaysian businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Amazon Web Services (AWS) said Malaysian software companies using its cloud platform to develop and deploy solutions recorded an average 30 per cent increase in cloud and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads between 2024 and 2025.
The growth indicates that local technology firms are handling larger computing workloads as they develop new digital products, enhance existing applications and integrate AI capabilities into solutions for businesses across various industries.
Recognising the importance of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in accelerating AI adoption, AWS said it is stepping up efforts to make the technology more accessible through local distribution channels, industry partnerships and established business networks.
The broader objective is to extend AI adoption beyond large corporations and government agencies, enabling SMEs, startups and local technology developers to benefit from the technology, improve productivity and create new business opportunities.
In a statement, AWS Malaysia country manager Hussein Mohd Ali said the nationwide Semarak AI Malaysia initiative was designed to accelerate the country's transition from being primarily a consumer of AI technology to becoming a developer and exporter of AI solutions, talent and intellectual property.
He said the programme would create a multiplier effect by encouraging government agencies, software companies and students to move beyond experimenting with AI towards developing and deploying their own solutions.
"When the public sector leads in building with AI, it becomes the lighthouse for the rest of the country. That's what Semarak AI Malaysia is designed to do; equip civil servants, software companies, and students with the tools to build their own AI solutions.
"Every ministry, every developer, and every student who builds with AI raises the bar for what's next," Hussein said.
As part of the initiative, AWS will make Amazon Quick, its AI assistant for work, available to up to 445,000 government officers through the National Digital Department's (JDN) AI-as-a-Service (AIaaS) platform.
The tool is expected to help civil servants automate routine administrative tasks and focus on higher-value activities, including analysing procurement data, synthesising policy research and identifying patterns across large datasets.
Wider adoption of AI could also benefit SMEs through improved inventory management, demand forecasting, automated customer service and personalised marketing, helping smaller businesses reduce operating costs, improve efficiency and compete more effectively.
Ultimately, AWS aims to strengthen Malaysia's digital ecosystem by developing local talent, encouraging homegrown innovation and enabling Malaysian companies to build solutions for both domestic and international markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Focus Point expands premium eyewear portfolio
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Focus Point Vision Care Group Sdn Bhd, Malaysia's largest optical retail chain, is strengthening its foothold in the premium eyewear market as part of its continued efforts to broaden its retail offerings and cater to the evolving preferences of discerning consumers.
The company, a subsidiary of Main Market-listed Focus Point Holdings Bhd, and which has a nationwide network of more than 210 outlets, has established a strong presence in Malaysia's optical retail industry.
Building on this foundation, it is now taking a strategic step into the luxury eyewear segment with the introduction of Focus Point Prestige, a dedicated retail concept designed to offer a more exclusive and elevated shopping experience.
The newly launched concept store brings together 14 international luxury eyewear brands under one roof.
The opening ceremony was attended by Johor Bahru Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Datuk Jeffrey Lai Jiun Jye, Focus Point Holdings Bhd president and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Liaw Choon Liang, and IGB REIT Management Sdn Bhd deputy CEO of retail Rennie Lee.
In a statement, Focus Point said the carefully selected portfolio reflects the diverse expressions of luxury eyewear, spanning Italian fashion heritage, French haute couture, Japanese precision engineering and contemporary design.
The launch reflects changing consumer expectations in Malaysia's eyewear market, where purchasing decisions increasingly extend beyond vision correction to include fashion, personal identity, comfort and product craftsmanship.
By combining luxury designer collections with professional eye care expertise and digital fitting technology, Focus Point aims to offer a more integrated retail experience for customers seeking both style and functional performance.
The initiative also reflects the group's broader strategy to strengthen its market positioning, expand its reach across different consumer segments and capture opportunities in the premium end of Malaysia's optical retail market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Bersatu skipped PN seat talks before fielding candidates, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu did not attend Perikatan Nasional's seat allocation negotiations before fielding candidates against the coalition in the Melaka election, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said.
He said Bersatu had been invited to participate in discussions on seat distribution ahead of the election but did not send any representatives.
The party later decided to field candidates against PN, despite maintaining that it remained part of the coalition.
"When we held the seat allocation meeting, we invited Bersatu, but they did not attend.
"They did not attend and then fielded candidates against PN candidates," he told reporters after attending the Ceramah Kelompok UDM Pantai Cheng last night.
He was responding to remarks by Bersatu vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu that
the party remained part of PN
.
Tuan Ibrahim also questioned Bersatu's commitment to the coalition, citing its complaint to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) seeking PN's deregistration.
"If they are still part of PN, they should not have lodged a report seeking to deregister the coalition.
"How can a component party lodge a complaint with the RoS to deregister PN and then claim that it is still part of the coalition? That is not right.
"If they were serious, they should not have lodged the complaint, and when we invited them to the meeting, they should have attended," he said.
He said the dispute over Bersatu's position within PN would ultimately be decided by the coalition's Supreme Council.
Meanwhile, Tuan Ibrahim expressed satisfaction with the progress of the election campaign, particularly the cooperation between Barisan Nasional and PN.
He said campaign activities had proceeded smoothly, with no major incidents reported apart from minor complaints involving party flags.
"I am satisfied with the progress of the campaign and very satisfied with the cooperation between BN and PN this time.
"I happened to meet Election Commission monitors, and the feedback I received was that campaigning has generally proceeded smoothly, without any serious incidents," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rapid KL train congestion: Anthony Loke vows fix after PM’s directive
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — The Transport Ministry is actively working to resolve train service congestion and overcome technical challenges faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
“Rapid KL is working to address various technical challenges. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service,” he said.
Loke told reporters this at his ministry’s get-together event with Tamil media practitioners at the Tropicana Golf and Country Resort here yesterday.
On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public’s daily routine.
The directive followed a complaint posted by a user on the Threads platform to Anwar regarding overcrowding at train stations.
Meanwhile, Loke said train frequencies have been increased for the festive season to encourage more people to use public transport when returning to their hometowns.
He said Electric Train Service (ETS) trips from Kuala Lumpur to west coast states, including Kedah and Johor, received an encouraging response, with additional services scheduled ahead of Deepavali.
“We have added trips ahead of Deepavali, and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is working to ensure service frequency is increased so that more people can take the train home,” he said.
Earlier, speaking on the event, Loke said it served as a platform to strengthen ties between the ministry and Tamil media practitioners in conjunction with Deepavali.
He noted that the media plays a vital role in disseminating information on ministry policies and services to all segments of society, including the Indian community.
Loke added that close cooperation with media practitioners is essential to ensure clear communication on road safety, public transport, the Road Transport Department (JPJ), and the aviation sector. — Bernama

Title: Heading east for Deepavali? Concessionaire releases travel time advisory for KLK and LPT1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Highway concessionaire AFA Prime Berhad has activated its Travel Time Advisory for the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) ahead of an anticipated holiday traffic surge for Deepavali.
The staggered travel schedule aims to ease bottlenecks across the arterial eastern corridor, particularly at the high-volume Gombak, Bentong, and Jabor toll plazas that link the Klang Valley to Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan.
Under its “Smart Travel” roadmap, the operator has segmented recommended departure windows by state destination to distribute traffic evenly across peak holiday dates.
For outbound journeys from Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Saturday, Nov 7, motorists passing through the Gombak Toll Plaza are advised to stagger their departures according to their destination.
Travellers heading to Kelantan are advised to start earliest, between 6am and 9am or from 5pm to 8pm.
Motorists bound for Terengganu should depart between 9am and 12pm or from 8pm to 11pm, while those heading to Pahang are urged to enter the expressway between 12pm and 4pm or during the secondary 8pm to 11pm window.
For the return commute towards the Klang Valley on Monday, Nov 9, drivers originating from Pahang are encouraged to use any toll plaza between 7am and 10am or from 7pm to 11pm.
Motorists returning from Terengganu through the Jabor Toll Plaza should target travel between 10am and 1pm or from 8pm to 10pm.
Meanwhile, traffic heading back from Kelantan via the Bentong Toll Plaza is advised to move between 4pm and 8pm or during the late 9pm to midnight slot.
To maximise efficiency, motorists are also encouraged to take advantage of “Free Travel Hours” during the midnight to 6am off-peak window on both designated dates.
Private car owners are specifically cautioned to avoid heavy express bus departure surges at the Gombak Toll Plaza, which peak between 9.30am and 12 noon as well as between 9.30pm and midnight.
AFA Prime managing director and chief executive officer Ahmad Faizi Latifi Ahmad Faiz reminded motorists to navigate cautiously through ongoing construction zones along the KLK, where active widening works are currently underway as part of the RM2.1 billion KLK Expansion project.
“We urge all road users to comply with the traffic instructions and signage at work zones, to reduce speed and to drive with extra care,” he said, adding that dedicated emergency response teams and patrol units will be deployed at strategic points along both expressways to provide rapid assistance.

Title: Anwar heads to Melaka to drum up Pakatan momentum ahead of Nov 14 polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend five programmes in Melaka tomorrow, including participating in Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign activities in conjunction with the Melaka State Election.
Anwar said two of the programmes he would be attending are the 2026 Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Award (MATEPM) ceremony and the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour.
“Insya-Allah, I will be in Melaka tomorrow for several engagements in this historic state. I will first visit Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) to meet educators and students at an official event, before heading to several other locations to boost the Harapan momentum in Melaka,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Based on the schedule shared in the post, Anwar is slated to begin his visit by attending the MATEPM 2026 at Dewan Canselor, UTeM, at 2.30 pm, before joining the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour for the Klebang state constituency in Taman Bukit Rambai at 4.45 pm.
In the evening, the PH chairman is scheduled to attend the ‘Malam Harapan’ programme at Dewan Pay Fong, SJK Pay Fong, at 7.30 pm, followed by the ‘Malam Ramah Mesra Melaka Rumah Kita Bersama PMX’ programme for the Paya Rumput constituency at Taman Seri Karanjong, Paya Rumput, at 8.30 pm.
Anwar is scheduled to conclude his visit by attending the ‘Sinar Deepavali Harapan’ celebration at Dewan Japerun Peringgit, Peringgit, at 9.30 pm.
Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Deepavali toll relief: 50pc discount on major highways this Friday and Saturday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Motorists travelling across the country for the Deepavali celebrations will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount on Friday and Saturday, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi announced today.
The festive waiver takes effect from 12.00am on Friday and concludes at 11.59pm on Saturday. Putrajaya estimates the two-day toll concession will require approximately RM20.11 million in federal compensation payouts to highway concessionaires, subject to post-holiday traffic volume verifications.
The discount applies to private Class 1 passenger vehicles across all interstate expressways, alongside Class 2 commercial vehicles crossing the Penang Bridge.
However, standard toll charges remain in force at the country’s two southern international border crossings: the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar (BSI) toll plaza on the North-South Expressway and the Tanjung Kupang toll plaza along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua).
“This decision reflects the MADANI Government’s continued concern and commitment to safeguarding the welfare and well-being of the people, regardless of race, religion or belief, while strengthening the spirit of unity and harmony within Malaysia’s multiracial society.
“This initiative is expected to help ease the people’s travel expenses, particularly for members of the Hindu community who return to their hometowns or visit family members to celebrate Deepavali, thereby giving greater meaning to the festive spirit through family ties and togetherness,” the minister said.
The Works Ministry, through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), will supervise operational coordination with all highway concessionaires to guarantee smooth implementation across automated lanes.
The ministry urged long-distance drivers to plan their travel times carefully to avoid peak bottleneck hours, maintain adequate credit balances in their Touch ‘n Go cards and RFID e-wallets, and track live traffic updates through LLM’s official monitoring channels.
Extending festive greetings to the Hindu community, the ministry expressed hope that the celebrations would foster warmth, harmony, and mutual respect across Malaysia’s multiracial society, while wishing all holidaymakers safe journeys to their hometowns.

Title: Seven foreigners held, RM1.08m in drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam raids
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 5 — Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1.
Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Division raided the premises at 12.50 am following surveillance and intelligence gathering.
“Police arrested six men and a woman, all aged between 25 and 38. Inspections of both premises uncovered MDMA powder and ketamine valued at an estimated RM1.08 million,” he said in a statement tonight.
