Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative. None of the suspects had prior criminal or drug-related records.
All suspects have been remanded for seven days from Nov 1 to 7 to assist in investigations under Section 39B, Section 12(3), and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Police are continuing investigations to track down the drug syndicate’s distribution network. — Bernama

Title: Penang ferry free for Malaysians on Nov 8 for Deepavali
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang Port Commission (PPC) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) will offer free ferry rides to Malaysian citizens on Nov 8 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration.
PPC chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the free ferry rides would be available to passengers departing from both Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Butterworth and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) in George Town.
“The free ferry service will operate according to the latest timetable. The public is advised to plan their journeys in advance and refer to the official websites and social media channels of PPC and PPSB for the latest ferry timetable,” he said in a statement.
Yeoh said the initiative reflected the continued commitment of PPC and PPSB to facilitating public travel, particularly during festive seasons, while helping to ease traffic congestion in Penang.
Citing figures from last year’s Deepavali celebration, Yeoh said 7,780 foot passengers and 1,518 two-wheeled vehicles used the ferry service in both directions.
He said the Penang ferry service also recorded a 5.61 per cent increase in passenger numbers from January to September this year compared with the corresponding period last year. — Bernama

Title: It is not a split, it is ‘policy deliberation’: Anwar cools talk of ministry feud over budgets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said differences of views between ministries do not necessarily reflect a split in the government but are part of policy deliberation, with matters needing a collective decision go to the Cabinet.
Anwar was replying in the Dewan Rakyat to Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin (Larut). Hamzah had asked whether an open contradiction between the Finance Ministry and the Rural and Regional Development Ministry showed a split in the government, and who determines its official position.
“The government wishes to stress that differences of views or approach between ministries do not necessarily reflect a split in the government,” Anwar said without naming either ministry or the specific matter in his reply.
“Rather, they are part of the process of discussion and policy deliberation, which takes into account each ministry’s responsibilities, jurisdiction and priorities, so that the MADANI Government’s agenda can be implemented effectively.”
The PM said the government ensures orderly coordination between ministries to keep policy consistent and avoid overlapping functions. He said every decision is made on the basis of the people’s interests, national development priorities and the government’s financial capacity.
On who decides the official position, Anwar said every government policy and decision must go through proper deliberation and coordination. He said matters requiring a collective decision are brought to the Cabinet for consideration and agreement, in line with the principle of collective Cabinet responsibility.
Anwar added that the government monitors economic performance continuously, using current data and indicators, to assess how well policies are working. He said this is also to keep strengthening the economy’s resilience against global uncertainty. He said the government will keep strengthening cooperation between ministries and monitor each initiative so that decisions deliver tangible and sustainable results.
The question follows a public disagreement over spending at the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, which is led by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid has rejected claims the ministry overspent by RM2.1 billion. Winding up the Budget 2027 debate on Oct 26, he said it spent RM6.108 billion from 2023 to 2025 against a revised allocation of RM6.143 billion, and had in fact underspent.
The issue drew attention after Zahid raised concern over delayed payments to contractors on ministry projects, saying some had been forced to stop operations because of cash flow problems.
Treasury secretary-general Datuk Seri Johan Mahmood Merican later attributed the delays to the ministry’s spending commitments, noting that most of this year’s allocation for rural road projects had already been used.

Title: Govt mulls three missile systems after Norway’s NSM permit cancellation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Ministry of Defence is in the final stages of evaluating three options for a surface-to-surface missile (SSM) system after the Norwegian government cancelled the export permit for the Naval Strike Missile (NSM).
The ministry said the selection of the system would take into account operational requirements, integration compatibility with naval vessels, costs and the procurement timeline.
“A final decision will be made once an option has been agreed upon and the procurement agreement has been signed,” the ministry said in a written reply to an oral question from Datuk Wira Dr Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (PN-Kubang Pasu) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
He had asked Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin to state the government’s measures to obtain the NSM system from another country following the Norwegian government’s cancellation of the export permit.
In a related development, the overall physical progress of the construction of all five Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) Littoral Combat Ships (LCS) stood at 80.72 per cent as of Sept 25, representing a delay variance of 9.19 per cent against the original target of 89.91 per cent.
According to the ministry, the latest delivery schedule guaranteed by the contractor, Lumut Naval Shipyard (LUNAS), stipulates that the first LCS will be delivered in April 2027, followed by the second in August 2027 and the third in December 2027.
The fourth LCS is scheduled for delivery in August 2028, while the fifth is set for April 2029.
As for the first LCS, KD Maharaja Lela, the vessel is currently undergoing Harbour Acceptance Trials after completing several shipyard acceptance tests.
The ministry said the trials involve testing the main machinery, power generation and propulsion systems to evaluate and verify the vessel’s performance and system capabilities before the Sea Acceptance Trials (SAT) are conducted together with RMN. — Bernama

Title: Carlsberg Malaysia says it was never a sponsor of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur, cites local laws and cultural sensitivities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Carlsberg Malaysia has clarified that it was never a sponsor of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 and holds no commercial involvement in the upcoming fitness competition, further defusing a controversy over marketing graphics that had drawn permit threats from the Youth and Sports Ministry.
In a statement posted to Instagram yesterday, the brewer explained that a newly unveiled regional partnership between Hyrox and Carlsberg in Asia applies exclusively to events staged in Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Vietnam, leaving Malaysia deliberately omitted from the arrangement.
“At Carlsberg Malaysia, we adhere to the country’s local laws, regulations, and respect cultural sensitivities,” the company said, reiterating its standard responsible consumption disclaimer that its products are strictly intended for non-Muslims aged 21 and above alongside the hashtag #CelebrateResponsibly.
The multi-day indoor fitness race is slated to take place from Dec 10 to 13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) in Kuala Lumpur.
The clarification came ahead of an ultimatum issued by the Youth and Sports Ministry on Wednesday, which warned that it would withhold operating approvals for the event until organisers completely purged the brewer’s branding, logos, and promotional assets from both physical venues and digital promotional channels.
The ministry noted that the organiser’s licence application remained pending and that Putrajaya had disbursed neither state funding nor regulatory clearance for the race.
Authorities cited Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code (3rd Edition, 2024), which explicitly prohibits tobacco, vape, and alcohol enterprises from sponsoring, advertising, or showcasing corporate trademarks across sporting events sanctioned by the ministry and its statutory agencies. Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari maintained that the government would brook no compromise in ensuring a healthy and safe sporting environment.
The ministry also cautioned organisers that proceeding with an unsanctioned competition violates Section 36(1) of the Sports Development Act 1997, which bars any entity from running sports activities without a formal licence from the Commissioner of Sports Malaysia, an offence punishable by fines up to RM500,000, a maximum five-year jail term, or both.
Hyrox Malaysia subsequently issued an apology across its social media channels, acknowledging that circulating the regional sponsorship graphic had caused distress and offense among the public.
Admitting that the management should have been more mindful of the religious beliefs and cultural norms of Malaysians, the organiser stated: “We got this wrong,” confirming that the decision to exclude Carlsberg from the Kuala Lumpur stop was made in mutual agreement with the brewer while reassuring registered participants that preparations for the race remain on track.

Title: KLIA altercation: Special Branch duo sue MCBA chief Shuhaily for assault, defamation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Two Special Branch policemen have filed a civil lawsuit against Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, suing him in his personal capacity for alleged assault, battery, false imprisonment, and defamation following an altercation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Dirman and Mohamad Faiz Muhamad Saman initiated the tort action at the Sepang Sessions Court yesterday, naming the border agency chief as the sole defendant while excluding the federal government from the suit,
NST
reported.
Their counsel, Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin, confirmed that the action pursues general, special, exemplary, and aggravated damages.
The civil lawsuit escalates the legal scrutiny surrounding Shuhaily, who was charged at the Sepang Magistrate's Court on Oct 21 with two criminal counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code. Shuhaily pleaded not guilty to both charges and remains out on court bail.
According to the statement of claim, both plaintiffs were deployed as Travel Control Officers at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28, tasked with security surveillance during Shuhaily's working visit to inspect border entry protocols for arriving Formula One contingents.
At around 1.27pm, the officers allegedly witnessed Shuhaily angrily confronting a civilian during a document check inside an enclosed inspection area near Counter J on Level 5.
Faiz captured photographs of the incident for internal intelligence logs, prompting MCBA deputy director-general for operations Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M. Nasir to seize the mobile phone before escorting both policemen directly to Shuhaily.
The plaintiffs alleged that upon discovering they were Special Branch personnel, Shuhaily grew incensed, questioned why police intelligence was monitoring MCBA personnel, and initiated a physical confrontation.
In their pleadings, the plaintiffs alleged that Shuhaily headbutted Ekmal four times before turning on Faiz, grabbing both of his ears and violently shaking his head, an ordeal that left them terrified and fearing for their physical safety.
The lawsuit also targets statements made by Shuhaily during a media briefing on Oct 1, accusing him of defaming the two officers by publicly implying that they had deliberately sabotaged border operations and recorded the altercation to tarnish the reputation of the agency and its leadership.
The plaintiffs contended that the remarks damaged their professional integrity and caused severe distress among their peers and families.

Title: Zahid: 2026 Cyber Crime Bill allows courts to freeze scam proceeds before suspects are charged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The 2026 Cyber Crime Bill provides powers for the court to issue property restriction orders to prevent scam proceeds from being dissipated, even before a suspect has been charged.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the provision under clause 54 enables the court to issue orders to prevent or stop violations of the law, thereby protecting victims of cybercrime.
“Among the orders that can be issued include cessation orders, restitution orders to victims, compliance orders, and property restriction orders to prevent assets such as scam proceeds from being dissipated,” he said in a written Dewan Rakyat reply yesterday.
He said that applications to obtain such orders can be submitted by the Public Prosecutor or an authorised officer.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, said the Bill - passed by Parliament last July - was formulated to tackle online scams utilising artificial intelligence (AI), including identity impersonation, deepfakes, and digital manipulation.
He was answering a question from Datuk Shamshulkahar Mohd Deli (BN-Jempol) regarding the adequacy of the existing legal framework to handle AI-based online fraud, as well as specific reinforced provisions to accelerate actions against syndicates and protect victims. — Bernama

Title: Learn from Trump’s midterm defeat: Guan Eng warns Putrajaya over ‘phantom growth’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — DAP’s Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the federal government to heed the political reckoning of the US midterm elections, warning that strong headline economic numbers will not save Putrajaya from voter backlash if everyday citizens continue to grapple with escalating living costs.
In a statement today, he pointed to the Republican Party's defeat in the Nov 3 polls, which saw Democrats seize control of the US Congress after voters rejected several of President Donald Trump’s endorsed candidates, including in longstanding conservative bastions.
Lim noted that despite the US registering 3.4 per cent gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026, voters remained unswayed because gains were concentrated in isolated sectors, creating a bifurcated two-tier economy that left ordinary households behind.
“Malaysia faces a similar two-tier economy. Despite a record 6 per cent GDP growth in the 2nd quarter 2026, many MSMEs and individuals complain about the so-called “phantom growth and controlled inflation” that fails to arrest their declining business or improve affordability and reduce the cost of living.
“These challenges are compounded by the government’s hike in compliance costs and taxes last year,” Lim said.
He contended that top-line expansion has done little to arrest declining sales volumes, relieve margin compression, or make daily necessities affordable, arguing that aggressive tax hikes and rising regulatory compliance burdens introduced by the government over the past year have only deepened commercial anxieties.
To bridge the divide, Lim called for direct engagement with struggling small business owners and employees across Malay, Chinese, and Indian communities.
He also took aim at bureaucrats heading statutory development agencies tasked with assisting small businesses, insisting they must “stop sleeping on the job” and actively champion policies that reduce operational friction and stimulate commerce.
Lim warned that while Malaysian leaders might feel indifferent toward Trump's political reversal, the underlying electoral dynamics are universal.
Disregarding public frustration over bread-and-butter struggles, he cautioned, will expose the ruling administration to an identical fate at the ballot box when the country next heads to the polls.

Title: Anwar: Hospital Seberang Jaya’s new cardiac services to cut waiting times, ease pressure on Penang Hospital
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — Hospital Seberang Jaya (HSJ) has made history as the first Level 2 hospital in Peninsular Malaysia to offer angiogram and angioplasty procedures, expanding access to specialised cardiac care for residents of Seberang Perai and surrounding areas.
Congratulating the hospital’s staff, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the expansion of services is expected to shorten waiting times and reduce the need for patients to seek treatment at Penang Hospital (HPP).
“Last January, I visited HSJ to officiate the hospital’s new building. Today’s development is certainly pleasing, as the upgraded facilities have now been followed by the expansion of specialised treatment urgently needed by residents in Seberang Perai and surrounding areas.
“My highest appreciation goes to the doctors, nurses, healthcare personnel, hospital management, and the Health Ministry (MOH) for this achievement. Your expertise and service bring hope to patients and strengthen public confidence in the country’s public healthcare sector,” he posted on social media last night.
Anwar said the Madani Government will continue to enhance the capabilities of public hospitals so that more people can receive faster access to quality treatment to protect lives and the people’s wellbeing.
Meanwhile, Penang State Cardiology Services head Datuk Dr Mohamed Jahangir Abdul Wahab said the operation of HSJ’s Invasive Cardiology Laboratory, which enables coronary angiogram and angioplasty procedures, reflects the government’s commitment to widening access to quality healthcare.
Dr Mohamed Jahangir, who is also HPP’s Cardiology Department head, said the initiative follows efforts by the Prime Minister and MOH to ensure more citizens have access to necessary specialised care.
According to him, the primary goal of expanding the service is to ensure patients receive quality cardiac care promptly and closer to home, without enduring long waits.
“With the rising burden of cardiovascular disease and the demand for increasingly complex cardiac care, expanding adult cardiology services at HSJ is a significant strategic step,” he told Bernama.
Dr Mohamed Jahangir said long-term plans are in place to develop HSJ into a more comprehensive heart treatment centre, which will include managing complex adult cardiology cases and introducing cardiothoracic surgical services targeted by mid-2027.
He said the initiative will not only increase cardiac treatment capacity in Penang, but also position HSJ as another major cardiovascular referral centre for the northern region of Peninsular Malaysia.
The development of adult cardiology services at HSJ has been carried out in phases since 2023, beginning with the posting of a resident cardiologist before being strengthened through regular specialist rotations, culminating in the establishment of the Cardiology Unit.
The unit is currently equipped with four Coronary Care Unit (CCU) beds and 15 Coronary Rehabilitation Ward (CRW) beds, alongside an Invasive Cardiology Laboratory fitted with an angiography system and modern electrophysiology equipment. — Bernama

Title: Fadillah says Melaka visit strictly for official business, not linked to state political developments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof has clarified that his presence in Melaka today was strictly on official business and has no connection to the state’s political developments.
Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister, said his visit was to officiate the 2026 CGNEI Gas Turbine Power Generation Committee Annual Conference at the EPH Training Centre, Edra Melaka Power Plant, in Kuala Sungai Baru.
In a statement yesterday, he said the conference is an energy generation programme that benefits the state’s economy and national energy security.
He noted that the conference, also attended by Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, is an initiative by CGN Energy International (CGNEI) and Edra Power Holdings Sdn Bhd through the establishment of the CGNEI Gas Turbine Skills Training Centre (CGNEI GTSTC) in Melaka.
“Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh’s presence at the event was also in his capacity as Chief Minister upon invitation by the organisers,” Fadillah said.
The statement was issued to set the record straight following attempts by certain quarters to link his presence at the event to current political developments in the state. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: RON95 quality, haze preparedness and maritime surveillance among key issues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The quality of RON95 petrol samples, mitigation of solid waste landfills, and enforcement against foreigners driving without valid licences are among the key issues slated for discussion in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) will ask the Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living to state the analysis outcome of RON95 samples across five states and depots during the Minister’s Question Time.
He is also seeking information on the government’s immediate measures to restore consumer confidence and the compensation for affected vehicle owners.
In the same session, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the Ministry of Housing and Local Government about the long-term strategy for critical open dumpsites under rural local authorities (PBT), as well as mitigation plans for districts without Waste-to-Energy (WTE) plants to curb daily waste accumulation.
Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) is scheduled to ask the Transport Minister to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms against foreigners, including United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders and undocumented immigrants driving motor vehicles without a valid licence, during the oral question-and-answer session.
Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) is scheduled to ask the Home Minister to state the progress of the early detection radar system, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), and satellite systems, the percentage of 24-hour surveillance coverage, and the asset capability gaps of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) that remain critical.
Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong) is also scheduled to ask about the government’s preparedness measures to prevent and address haze episodes, as the El Nino phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027.
At the conclusion of the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will continue with the committee stage debate and ministerial replies for the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 and the Motion on the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates.
The committee stage debate and winding-up session for Budget 2027 is scheduled to run until Nov 26, according to the Dewan Rakyat calendar.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to sit for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Can monthly EPF withdrawals keep retirees from running out of money?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — For many Malaysians, retirement savings are built up over decades of working life, but the challenge does not end when they reach retirement age as they must then make that money last for the rest of their lives.
The government is encouraging Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members to consider taking their savings through monthly withdrawals instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once, with the aim of helping them manage their finances and preserve their retirement income for longer.
Under Budget 2027, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that EPF members aged 55 and 60 could opt for monthly withdrawals under the i-Emas scheme, allowing savings retained with the fund to continue earning annual dividends.
The arrangement offers an alternative to taking out the full balance at once, but economists and financial experts say the wider question is whether changing how retirees withdraw their money will be enough to address Malaysia’s retirement savings problem.
Lee Heng Guie, an economist, said a survey had found that about 97 per cent of Malaysians withdrew their EPF savings in a lump sum at age 55 or 60, with many depleting the money within three to five years.
He said monthly withdrawals could help reduce the risk of retirees exhausting their savings too quickly by encouraging more disciplined spending while allowing the unwithdrawn balance to continue earning dividends.
“Besides continuing to earn dividends on the unwithdrawn savings, a structured schedule of withdrawals instils disciplined spending to reduce the risk of mismanaging lump-sum withdrawals,” he said.
For retirees who depend on their EPF savings to cover daily expenses, the distinction could be significant: money withdrawn and spent no longer earns returns within the fund, while savings left invested can continue generating dividends.
Samsudin Kadir, an economist, similarly argued that most retirees did not need their entire retirement savings immediately, but instead required a regular stream of income to meet household expenses.
He said monthly payouts could be particularly useful for people who did not have substantial savings or the financial knowledge to manage a large sum independently.
“If you withdraw everything, because normally people do not know how to manage the money lump sum,” he said.
Samsudin added that a retirement income system should still allow access to additional funds when members faced illness or other exceptional circumstances.
However, Stewart Nixon, director of research at the Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (IDEAS), cautioned that monthly withdrawals alone would not necessarily solve the problem of inadequate retirement income.
He argued that the government must also consider whether EPF delivers sufficient investment returns and whether members have the flexibility to manage their savings according to their individual needs.
“The top consideration should be whether the new model actually improves retirement living standards,” he said.
Stewart said a structured withdrawal system could help people who struggled to manage their finances, but warned against making it harder for others to pursue better investment options.
“The single biggest impediment to Malaysians having enough money in retirement is that they are locked into EPF arrangements that deliver suboptimal long-term returns,” he said.
He argued that giving members more investment choice, improving financial literacy and ensuring EPF maximises risk-appropriate returns were important to improving retirement adequacy.
Stewart also said Malaysia should prioritise developing a competitive, properly regulated annuity market, which would allow retirees to convert some of their savings into a guaranteed income stream for life.
Such arrangements could help retirees manage the risk of outliving their savings, although he cautioned that annuity products would require careful regulation to protect consumers from predatory practices.
Flexibility remains crucial
While the three experts broadly recognised the potential benefits of regular withdrawals, they differed on how far the system should go in steering members away from lump-sum payments.
Samsudin supported a model that combined monthly income with limited lump-sum withdrawals at different stages of retirement, arguing that no single arrangement would suit everyone.
He said retirees should be able to access additional money when faced with significant medical expenses, while those with different income levels and financial commitments should have options suited to their circumstances.
Lee likewise acknowledged that regular withdrawals had limitations, particularly when retirees faced unexpected financial pressures, rising living costs, inflation or escalating healthcare expenses.
He pointed to EPF’s Flexible Account, or Akaun Fleksibel, which allows members to withdraw available savings for short-term needs, as one existing avenue for accessing money when required.
Stewart, meanwhile, argued that some retirees could be better served by taking a lump sum to settle high-interest debts, while financially capable individuals might be able to achieve better returns through other investments.
The challenge, therefore, is to ensure that a system designed to protect retirement savings does not leave members without sufficient access to their own money when circumstances demand it.
Monthly withdrawals may help retirees avoid spending too much too soon, but they cannot by themselves guarantee a comfortable retirement if the savings accumulated during their working years is inadequate.
Ultimately, the question facing policymakers is whether encouraging retirees to draw down their savings more gradually will be enough — or whether Malaysia needs a more fundamental overhaul of how retirement income is generated, invested and protected throughout old age.

Title: Brickfields Deepavali traders turn to TikTok as shoppers shun relocated bazaar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — After weeks of sluggish sales, Deepavali bazaar traders in Brickfields are making a final push on TikTok to drive last-minute sales ahead of the festival on Sunday.
Unlike previous years, the stalls are no longer scattered along the main roads of Brickfields.
This year, they have been moved off the main road to ease traffic congestion.
The shops are now housed under sturdy marquee tents at the Kompleks Tun Sambanthan car park, sheltering them and their goods from strong winds and torrential rain.
Yet many here long for their old spots, where they say business was far better.
Gunaseelan Subramaniam, a clothing vendor who has traded at the Brickfields Deepavali bazaar for 25 years, said his old spot drew a stronger crowd during breakfast and lunch hours on working days.
Gunaseelan Subramaniam, a clothing vendor at the Deepavali bazaar in Brickfields said he hardly made RM1,000 during his last weekend sale. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
“The footfall was better there on the main road. A lot of tourists visited my shop in the previous years and in fact, I had a strong crowd of Malay customers.
“This year, people barely knew the bazaar exists here,” he told Malay Mail when met at his stall recently.
“Our best sales are usually on the last weekend before Deepavali, but I hardly earned even RM1,000 over the three days last week.”
Desperate to boost sales, Gunaseelan went live on TikTok to promote the bazaar and appeal for public support.
“I had some customers who said they used to walk past this area but didn’t know the bazaar was operating here until the TikTok videos went viral.
“It’s the only thing keeping us afloat for now,” he said.
Having traded here since 2022, Sunita Gill from Ipoh said she may not return to the Brickfields Deepavali bazaar next year unless traders are relocated to their old spots. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Viswalingam Karuppiah, 61, who sells traditional wear sourced directly from India, said shoppers were reluctant to bring their children to the bazaar due to the sweltering heat inside the tents.
Only a few air coolers were installed along the bazaar corridors, which he said was insufficient to keep the area cool.
“We are thankful to Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) for lowering the rent to just RM400 per lot and giving us sturdy tents.
“But people come to the bazaar for clothes because they want to feel the material and try it on before buying.
“Nobody wants to stay here too long because it is so hot, even at night,” he said.
Like Gunaseelan, Viswalingam has also turned to TikTok to attract customers as he races against time to recover his capital.
Viswalingam Karuppiah, 61, said fewer families come to the bazaar to shop due to the sweltering heat inside the tents. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Meanwhile, trader Sunita Gill from Ipoh has seen her hopes dashed as her kurtis and lenghas have struggled to leave the racks since the bazaar opened a month ago.
Sunita, a full-time homemaker, had hoped to repeat the strong sales she recorded at last year’s bazaar.
“At my old spot opposite the RHB Bank, I could easily sell two to three dresses during lunch hour alone. But this year, I have hardly made 10 per cent of what I earned last year,” she said.
Having traded here since 2022, Sunita said she will most likely not return to the Brickfields Deepavali bazaar next year unless traders are relocated to their old spots.
“I’d rather take another location. I won’t be here because business here is very bad.”
Deepavali falls on November 8 this year.

Title: Fadhlina warns of ‘scrolling generation’ as gadgets erode reading habits among youth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The emergence of digital gadgets has increasingly undermined reading habits among younger generations, giving rise to a “scrolling generation”, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said reading should be part of everyday life, rather than merely a leisure activity, to nurture a more knowledgeable generation.
“One book that is particularly popular at the moment is
The New Dark Ages
, which has also caught the attention of the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), who has discussed it himself.
“
The New Dark Ages
depicts a deep sense of fear surrounding the generation described as the ‘scrolling generation’,” she said in her speech at the closing ceremony of the HIPMaX Malaysian Folklore Storyfest: Folktales Reimagined Grand Finale Showcase 2026 at the National Library of Malaysia (PNM) here today.
Also present were Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh, Deputy Director-General of Education (Policy and Curriculum Sector) Dr Rusmini Ku Ahmad, and PNM director-general Edy Irwan Zulkafli.
Fadhlina said encouraging a reading culture among Malaysians, particularly students at schools and universities, was a key government priority, adding that the ministry introduced the ‘Jom Baca Bersama 10 Minit’ programme to promote reading among pre-school, primary and secondary school pupils.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina expressed hope that the HIPMaX Malaysian Folklore Storyfest would continue to foster a love of reading among pupils while introducing them to folk tales that reflect the country’s history, culture and identity. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Price of RON97 down by 20 sen, RON95 and diesel drop by 15 sen respectively tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The retail price of RON97 has dropped by 20 sen to RM4.70 per liter, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel have both dropped 15 sen to RM4.27 and RM5.12 per liter respectively for the period of November 5 to 11.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF), in a statement today, announced that this pricing is determined based on the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula, compared to the current prices of RM4.90 for RON97, RM4.42 for unsubsidised RON95, and RM5.27 for unsubsidised diesel.
“The regional petroleum market shows signs of moderation following an increase in the supply of refined fuels, including petrol and diesel stocks in Singapore, which serves as one of the market references for petroleum pricing in Malaysia.
“This development, together with the drop in Brent crude oil prices at the end of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, indicates the possibility of lower price pressures,” according to the statement.
However, MOF noted that geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia continue to pose risks to world petroleum price stability.
Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 through Budi95 remains at RM1.99 per liter, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.28 per liter, or 53 percent of the unsubsidised price for the period.
For Budi Diesel, the price for eligible recipients remains at RM2.10 per liter, involving a government subsidy of RM3.02 per liter, or 59 percent of the unsubsidised price.
Additionally, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remains at RM2.05 per liter, while diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.15 per liter.
According to the MOF, eligible Malaysians can continue to purchase subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to monthly eligibility limits.
“The Madani Government will continue to take a prudent approach to protect the rakyat from price fluctuations, while ensuring that the country’s fuel supply remains adequate and secure,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: Penang e-hailing drivers to get one-off RM600 aid from 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — A one-off payment of RM600 for e-hailing drivers in Penang will be disbursed in 2027, with applications opening in January 2027 through the i-Sejahtera system.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the application criteria for the Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance would be announced next month.
“E-hailing services have become an important component of the urban transport system, supporting first- and last-mile connectivity while providing the public with flexible mobility services.
“In line with the Unity Manifesto that was announced, a payment of RM600 will be disbursed in 2027, with applications to be submitted through the i-Sejahtera system,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates (State Budget 2027) at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, when tabling the 2027 State Budget on Friday (Oct 30), announced that the state government would introduce a one-off Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance of RM600 for eligible drivers, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million.
In a separate development, Zairil said the state government had submitted an application to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for RM750 million in funding under the Universal Service Provision (USP) Fund to implement the Communication Infrastructure and Digital Connectivity for Penang Smart City initiative.
He said the proposed initiative included the development of about 290 kilometres of fibre-optic network, mainly in Seberang Perai, the expansion of last-mile facilities and communication tower infrastructure and connectivity support for private 5G networks.
He said it would also involve the development of a Network Operations Centre (NOC), artificial intelligence (AI)-based smart asset monitoring and provision of high-speed public WiFi facilities to strengthen the state’s overall digital capabilities.
“As such, the state government hopes that MCMC will give due consideration to and subsequently approve this application for funding to enable the initiative to be implemented in Penang.
“Approval of the allocation will serve as a catalyst for the development of more integrated and resilient digital infrastructure, thus enhancing the state’s capacity to navigate technological advancements,” he added.
The State Legislative Assembly sitting will resume tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Mutiara Line LRT link to Penang Sentral to begin construction in 2027, completion targeted for 2031
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Construction of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) alignment linking Macallum on the island to Penang Sentral in Seberang Perai, including a marine bridge across the Penang Strait, is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the tender evaluation process for the alignment was currently being undertaken by MRT Corp, the implementing agency, and was expected to be completed this month.
“Construction is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, following the appointment of the main contractor for the Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment. Preliminary works will be carried out first, followed by major construction activities, including the construction of a bridge across the Penang Strait.
“The alignment is targeted for completion by December 2031, in tandem with the section linking Silicon Island to Komtar on the island,” he said in a written reply during the State Assembly sitting here today.
He was responding to a question from Kumaran Krishnan (PH-Bagan Dalam) on the commencement of the LRT alignment in Seberang Perai, particularly the section leading to Penang Sentral.
Zairil said the finalised Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment would feature a 5.5-kilometre (km) marine bridge across the Penang Strait, with two main stations at Macallum and Penang Sentral.
The Bagan Luar station, meanwhile, has been designated as a provisional station to facilitate possible future expansion of the alignment.
The Mutiara Line LRT project is scheduled to begin construction in 2025, with operations expected to commence in December 2031. The line will span approximately 29.67 km and comprise 20 stations, in addition to two provisional stations.
As the first integrated metro transit system in the northern region, the project is expected to improve connectivity between Penang Island and the mainland, ease traffic congestion and enhance accessibility. — Bernama

Title: In Johor, six-year-old boy drowns after falling into reservoir while fishing
Article:
KULAI, Nov 4 — A six-year-old boy drowned after falling into a reservoir while fishing at Jalan Budiman in Kampung Melayu Kulai here today.
Kulai Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Awang Adzwan Awang Sahari said authorities received a distress call on the incident at 10.17am.
He said six personnel, assisted by an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit, were immediately dispatched to the scene that was located four kilometres from the fire station.
“Upon arrival, the responding team discovered that a boy had fallen into the reservoir and was believed to have drowned,” he said in a statement today.
Awang Adzwan said the team located the victim and carried out a rescue operation.
He said the team employed the use of ropes and a stretcher to retrieve the victim from the reservoir.
The victim, who is a Primary One pupil, was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant.
The operation concluded at 11.25am.

Title: Over five million Malaysians to receive RM1.1b STR aid from today, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The fourth phase of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid, amounting to RM1.1 billion, is being disbursed starting today to over five million recipients nationwide, as part of ongoing efforts to assist the public in coping with the pressure of the cost of living.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the disbursement is being made in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration and covers recipients from various ethnic backgrounds.
He noted that this assistance reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that the welfare of the people particularly those in the low-income group remains a priority.
“Therefore, in conjunction with Deepavali, I am announcing that from today until November 6, a total of RM1.1 billion in STR aid will be distributed to more than five million people,” he said while speaking during a visit to the Deepavali Mega Bazaar 2026 in Brickfields here today.
Also present were Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Minister of Digital Gobind Singh Deo.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, emphasised that the STR (Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah) assistance is not focused on any specific ethnic group, instead it is open to all citizens who meet the eligibility criteria.
He noted that the Indian community also benefits from this initiative, with over 630,000 recipients accounting for 7.4 per cent of the total number of STR recipients nationwide.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said the government’s cash assistance allocation has grown from RM6 billion under the “Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia” (BR1M) scheme in 2018 to RM8 billion under the “Bantuan Keluarga Malaysia” (BKM) scheme in 2022.
He added that this figure is set to rise to RM15 billion for STR and “Sumbangan Asas Rahmah” (SARA) allocations in 2026, before increasing further to RM16 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He remarked that this increase in allocation demonstrates the government’s commitment to strengthening the social safety net and ensuring that aid reaches those in need.
“So, you can make comparisons. You can also express gratitude. Some might say, ‘It existed before, too.’ That is true. But how much was it back then? RM6 billion. And how much is it now? RM16 billion for the people especially those in the lowest income bracket,” he said.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, the Ministry of Finance said STR payments to existing recipients will be processed from November 4 to 6, while new recipients and those whose appeals were approved will receive their payments starting November 16.
Of this total, 4.0 million are households with an income of RM5,000 or less, while 1.4 million are senior citizens without a spouse.
Based on eligibility categories, households will receive up to RM500, while senior citizens without a spouse will receive RM150.
MOF also said recipients with bank accounts will receive payments via direct credit to their respective accounts, while those without bank accounts may collect their payments in cash at any Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) branch.
Further information, status checks, and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding the STR can be accessed via the official portal at bantuantunai.hasil.gov.my, while information concerning SARA (Sumbangan Asas Rahmah) can be found at sara.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Selangor gears up for north-east monsoon, deploys 7,677 personnel for disaster response
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — The Selangor state government has mobilised 7,677 personnel from various state agencies to prepare for disasters during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March 2027.
State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the mobilisation involved the State Disaster Management Unit (UPBN), local authorities, district offices and relevant agencies to coordinate operations and monitor high-risk areas.
In a statement today, she said the operation was supported by 708 land vehicles, 247 water transport assets and various rescue equipment, including 5,739 tents, 1,950 life jackets, 141 water pumps and 20 drones.
According to the Selangor Drainage and Irrigation Department (JPS), the state is expected to receive 2,232 millimetres of rainfall this year, with 1,460 mm, or 65 per cent, recorded as at November 1. Rainfall of 268 mm and 230 mm is forecast for November and December respectively.
Jamaliah said JPS was monitoring flood risks through 221 rainfall telemetry stations, 124 water-level monitoring stations, 140 warning sirens and 72 IP cameras.
Based on 2025 data, JPS had identified 56 flood hotspots and 232 flood-prone areas, with Klang recording the highest number of hotspots at 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10) and Hulu Langat (nine).
She also cautioned residents in coastal and river estuary areas of Klang, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Langat, Sabak Bernam and Kuala Selangor about the risk of high tides.
Meanwhile, 1,161 temporary relief centres (PPS) had been identified statewide, including 696 schools under the Education Ministry, 242 public halls and 135 community halls.
Jamaliah said agencies had been instructed to ensure the centres were safe, equipped with basic facilities and sufficient food supplies, while giving due attention to vulnerable groups.
She advised residents to monitor weather alerts through the JPS Public InfoBanjir portal and the Malaysian Meteorological Department’s (MET Malaysia) myCuaca 3.0 application, and comply with evacuation orders. — Bernama

Title: Klang Valley raids uncover suspected luxury liquor tax-stamp scam, RM702,566 haul seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Police have uncovered a suspected tax-stamp diversion scheme involving luxury liquor following the seizure of 370 bottles worth RM702,566 in the Klang Valley on Monday and yesterday.
The operation, Ops Taring Alpha 2, was conducted by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) of the Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Customs Department.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the liquor, packed in 73 boxes, was seized during separate raids at a warehouse in Selangor and business premises in the capital.
He said initial inspections at the warehouse found that some luxury liquor bottles allegedly bore tax stamps or customs labels with lower duty rates than those applicable to the products.
“The modus operandi is believed to involve the diversion of tax stamps to evade excise duty payments, potentially resulting in revenue leakage,” he said in a statement today.
However, inspections at the second premises found that all liquor bottles bore valid tax stamps, with no offences detected.
Mohd Zaki said four individuals, including three Bangladeshis, were arrested to assist investigations under Section 15(1)(c) and Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Regulation 39(B) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
The Customs Department is also investigating possible offences under Section 133(1)(c) of the Customs Act 1967. — Bernama

Title: Three boat operators among 38 Indonesians held in Selangor migrant smuggling crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Three boat operators were among 38 Indonesian nationals detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) in an operation to curb migrant smuggling along the coastal area of Kampung Sungai Gatal, near Sabak Bernam, on November 2.
GOF Central Brigade acting commander ACP Awang Arfian Awang Bujang said all of them were detained in a raid under Op Taring Delta at about 4.30am while they were believed to be attempting to leave Malaysia via an illegal sea route.
He said the other 35 individuals arrested comprised 24 adult men and 11 adult women.
“The operations team also seized a fishing boat, a Mitsubishi engine and three mobile phones of various brands, which are believed to have been used as communication devices in the smuggling operation.
“The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM406,800,” he told a press conference here today.
He said the case was being investigated under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM) and the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Awang Arfian said the GOF Central Brigade recorded 171 cases involving migrant smuggling activities and immigration offences from January 1 to November 4 this year.
He said enforcement operations during the period led to the arrest of 898 individuals in the brigade’s area of responsibility, which covers Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor.
“Of the total, 33 cases were investigated under ATIPSOM, involving the arrest of 76 boat operators, while another 138 cases were recorded under the Immigration Act 1959/63, with 822 arrests,” he said.
He said the GOF would continue to intensify operations and intelligence gathering to combat migrant smuggling and other illegal cross-border activities.
“Members of the public with information on such activities are urged to channel it to the police for further action,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says aid for Indian community goes beyond Mitra, more initiatives in pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Government assistance for the Indian community is not only channelled through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), but also includes various initiatives in welfare, entrepreneurship, education and social development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said such assistance was also provided through various government agencies and programmes, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid scheme, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), entrepreneurship financing through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, as well as allocations for the development of Tamil schools and places of worship.
“Sometimes, people think that the only assistance available for the Indian community is MITRA, whereas there are also STR, Amanah Ikhtiar, and Tekun (Nasional)... all of these are also part of the support we provide.
“Is this enough? Not yet. That I agree, but we are gradually increasing. We are discussing this constructively to introduce new initiatives where there were none before,” he said during a visit to the Brickfields Deepavali Mega Bazaar 2026 here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Anwar, also the Finance Minister, said Mitra’s annual allocation, which has stood at RM100 million since 2008, has been increased to RM150 million, which is a 50 per cent rise.
He said priority would be given to skills training programmes and employment opportunities for young members of the Indian community, particularly in industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance.
The government is also expanding financing facilities through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, with an additional RM150 million allocated to assist entrepreneurs from the Indian community.
In the education sector, Anwar said the allocation for repair and maintenance works at Tamil National-Type Schools (SJKT) had been increased to RM50 million, with priority given to dilapidated schools and those requiring urgent attention.
He said the government also planned to fully rebuild SJKT Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor, as well as establish six new SJKTs, including in Sungai Bakap, Penang and Klebang, Perak.
Meanwhile, the allocation for the maintenance and development of registered places of worship was also increased to RM80 million next year, compared with RM50 million annually since 2021.
“This form of assistance existed previously, but under the Madani Government, it has been increased in stages following discussions and assessments of the community’s needs,” Anwar added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian prosecutors unable to find Yusoff Rawther in UK to physically serve appeal notice despite Interpol help
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — The Court of Appeal was told today that the prosecution has yet to physically serve a notice of appeal on Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, a former research assistant to a politician, who is currently in the United Kingdom (UK).
Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) How May Ling told a three-member panel that authorities in the UK and Ireland had failed to locate Muhammed Yusoff or serve the notice on him, despite assistance being sought from Interpol.
“The prosecution was informed last month that efforts to locate the respondent (Muhammed Yusoff) had been unsuccessful. The authorities also had no information regarding his asylum application,” she said during case management before Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and K. Muniandy.
The prosecution is appealing against the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Muhammed Yusoff of charges of trafficking cannabis and possessing two imitation pistols at the end of the prosecution’s case, without calling him to enter his defence.
How said the respondent’s counsel had informed the court during an earlier proceeding that they were still in contact with him and had received instructions to represent him in the appeal.
The DPP said the prosecution was seeking another case management date to allow efforts to locate Muhammed Yusoff and serve the notice to continue.
It also applied for the proceedings to be conducted via Zoom so that he could appear online and confirm his whereabouts in the UK, facilitating service of the appeal notice.
On the Zoom application, Justice Azman said the case should not be treated differently from other criminal cases.
“I do not want to make an exception in this case. This is a criminal proceeding, and the respondent must appear physically in court. This court also does not want to set an unnecessary precedent.
“If the prosecution succeeds in locating him, bring him before this court,” he said.
Justice Azman also urged the lawyer to advise his client to return to Malaysia, given that they had a channel of communication with him.
Counsel Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, representing Muhammed Yusoff, said he acknowledged that physical service of the appeal notice was a legal requirement under Section 314 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
However, he maintained that his client was not on the run but was in the UK to seek asylum.
The court fixed February 3 next year for further case management.
On June 12, 2025, High Court Judge Datuk Muhammad Jamil Hussin acquitted and discharged Muhammed Yusoff, 33, after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him.
The court found that the prosecution had failed to prove, through witness testimony, that the accused had control, custody or possession of the two pistols and the drugs.
Muhammed Yusoff was charged with trafficking 305 grammes of cannabis found in a vehicle he was travelling in outside the surau at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters at 10.15am on September 6, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, which provides for life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction.
He was also charged with possessing two imitation pistols by the roadside near a condominium in Jalan Bukit Kiara at 9.25am on the same day.
The charge was under Section 36(1) of the Arms Act 1960, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Penang DOSH to probe cause of fatal Paya Terubong landslide, developer told to submit documents
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is conducting an investigation to determine the actual cause of the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, covering aspects such as safety, construction, and regulatory compliance.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the investigation includes gathering information and statements from the developer, contractors, and consultants involved in the development project on the slope near the site of the incident.
“The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) held discussions yesterday (Nov 3) with civil and geotechnical consulting engineers, the developer, and the contractor to investigate and understand the root cause of the incident covering aspects of safety, construction, design, and compliance with relevant regulations as well as to propose appropriate mitigation measures and site stabilization efforts.
“DOSH has requested that the developer submit Pre-Construction Information (PCI) documentation before commencing any mitigation work on-site,” he said when winding the debate on the Supply Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates (State Budget 2027) at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
In the incident on October 25, a doctor, Dr Wong Kar Lin, 73, died after being buried in a landslide that affected his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim (in her 80s), managed to escape safely.
Elaborating further, H’ng said the approved 35-story affordable housing project near the site does not exceed the 76-metre (250-foot) contour line while infrastructure development such as roads and utilities is permitted, subject to strict conditions outlined in the geotechnical report approved by the Committee for Development on Risky Land on April 10, 2023.
Additionally, he explained that the development approval for the site dates back to 1996, when the initial developer submitted an application for a proposed project consisting of medium-cost apartments and townhouses.
The planning permission application subsequently underwent several changes in terms of the developer and the proposed development plan before... The application for planning permission for the development of the affordable housing project was submitted in 2023.
“I wish to emphasise here that all decisions made were collective decisions of the government not merely the decision of the Chief Minister, but rather those of the State Authority and the Local Authority,” he stated.
In response to a query from Muhammad Fauzi Yusoff (PN-Sungai Dua), who interjected to urge the establishment of a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) to investigate the cause of the tragedy, H’ng said the state government would first defer the investigation process to the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) before considering such a measure.
He explained that the relevant documentation must be examined by DOSH, with technical advice sought from the Engineering Department of the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) specifically regarding geotechnical aspects to ensure that the proposed mitigation works are appropriate, before any further action is taken.
Previously, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow asserted that the landowner and the developer of the condominium project must be held accountable, including regarding legal implications and the implementation of mitigation works to ensure the safety of the area affected by the landslide. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest 35 foreigners in Penang love scam, gold investment fraud raids
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Police arrested 35 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in an online fraud syndicate specialising in love scams and gold investment schemes during raids on two residences in Bayan Lepas, near here, last Monday.
Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said the suspects, comprising 33 Chinese men, one Chinese woman and one Taiwanese man, were arrested in an operation conducted by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division in collaboration with the Penang Contingent Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID).
“Preliminary investigations revealed that the syndicate began operating last September, targeting Chinese national women aged between 18 and 46 through the Telegram application,” he said in a statement today.
He said police also seized 119 mobile phones, three laptops and chargers, believed to have been used to facilitate the syndicate’s activities, with the total estimated value of the seized items amounting to RM60,000.
All the suspects are on remand to assist in investigations under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code.
In another development, Anuwal said police were conducting further investigations into an accident involving a Rapid Penang bus and a motorcycle along Jalan Mayang Pasir, near here, last night, which claimed the life of a 29-year-old motorcyclist.
He said police were recording witness statements, reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and examining the vehicles involved to assist in investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, relating to causing death by reckless or dangerous driving. — Bernama
